query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying with oxygen-resistant elements can improve the high-temperature performance of Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.intervention: Addition of 1-2 at.% Aluminum to form a protective oxide layer
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 100 hours, Mechanical-loading boundaries: Strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective Al2O3 layer
generation.mechanism: The added Aluminum reacts with oxygen to form a thin, dense, and adherent Al2O3 layer, reducing oxidation and improving resistance to high-temperature degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: 20-50% increase in yield strength and 10-20% increase in tensile ductility at 1000 °C, with minimal loss of room-temperature mechanical properties
generation.baseline: Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr with 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and 163–530 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C
generation.boundary: Strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, exposure time of 100 hours, and temperature of 1000 °C
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Aluminum addition required to achieve optimal performance without sacrificing mechanical properties is uncertain

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of 1-2 at.% Aluminum does not result in a significant improvement in yield strength and tensile ductility at 1000 °C, or if the oxidation rate is not reduced, then the hypothesis is falsified
